description: Curated theme/subtheme commentary — manually-captured trader theses, lead-lag relationships, and ticker linkages. Read by SUBFLOW (eventually) for context overlays.

notes.headline: VIAV + FORM beats → bullish capex read for HBM / advanced packaging / optical ramps

lead_lag.rationale: Capex on test/inspection equipment leads device-maker production ramps by 1-2Q. Test margin expansion (FORM 49% gross) implies capacity-constrained pricing power — i.e., real ramp incoming.

caveats: TOWA is 6315.T (Tokyo) — not in FMP live feed, won't surface in SUBFLOW.
Test/inspection thesis assumes ramp follows; tariff or memory-pricing reversal could break the chain.

notes.headline: MSFT/META/AMZN Q1 capex print: upstream semi supply chain stays bullish through 2026

MSFT.miss_reason: Supply chain bottlenecks, NOT demand pullback
MSFT.read_through: Bullish — capex constrained by upstream supply, demand intact

lead_lag.rationale: Hyperscaler capex commitments funnel directly into semi capex (foundry → equipment → test/inspection). MSFT capex 'miss' is on the supply side, which means equipment/test names absorb the unmet demand. Reinforces the VIAV/FORM/ONTO/CAMT thesis from earlier today.

caveats: Capex guides can be revised down if AI ROI doesn't materialize — watch for hyperscaler deceleration in Q2/Q3 prints.
AMZN AWS margin compression risk if capex pace doesn't translate to revenue — different bull case than META/MSFT.

notes.headline: AMZN Jassy: memory/storage costs skyrocketed, capacity insufficient — accelerates custom silicon shift

key_quotes.speaker: Andy Jassy (AMZN CEO)
key_quotes.quote: Memory and storage costs have skyrocketed, with memory under the most pressure. There isn't enough capacity for current demand.

implications: Memory pricing: confirmed supply-constrained — bullish MU / SNDK / WDC.
Custom silicon acceleration: hyperscalers pushing toward in-house ASIC over off-the-shelf — bullish AVGO (Trainium/Google TPU) and MRVL (custom).
Cost-efficient infrastructure focus: optical interconnect ROI matters more — 1.6T pluggables / co-packaged optics still in the chain.
Confirms the upstream-semi-supply-chain thesis from META/MSFT prints — capacity, not demand, is the constraint.

lead_lag.rationale: Memory capacity tightness + custom-silicon shift is a multi-quarter call. HBM probe-card demand (FORM) and inspection (ONTO/CAMT) tighten further as memory fab utilization climbs.

caveats: If memory pricing peaks and rolls (cycle behavior), MU/SNDK could top before equipment names — watch DRAM contract pricing trends.
Custom silicon shift hurts NVDA share-of-wallet at the margin, even if the overall pie grows.

notes.headline: All four hyperscalers (MSFT/META/GOOGL/AMZN) said the same thing: 'power and compute constrained'

key_quotes.speaker: MSFT
key_quotes.quote: We are power and compute constrained

key_quotes.speaker: META
key_quotes.quote: We are power and compute constrained

key_quotes.speaker: GOOGL
key_quotes.quote: We are power and compute constrained

key_quotes.speaker: AMZN
key_quotes.quote: We are power and compute constrained

implications: Power side: every IPP / nuclear / grid / electrical-equipment name has multi-year visibility. Datacenter demand is hitting the grid faster than utilities can build.
Compute side: confirms the upstream semi thesis — bottleneck is supply, not demand. Capex flows into foundry/equipment/test, not Q-on-Q AI revenue.

Stack ranking matters: companies that solve BOTH constraints (e.g., Coreweave-style power+compute combos, hyperscalers with PPA pipelines like MSFT/CEG) win. Pure-compute plays without power answer get capped.
Power becomes the new capex line item. When all four say it in unison, that's when allocators start reweighting from semis toward power.

lead_lag.rationale: Power buildout is a 2-5 year cycle (permitting, transmission, generation). Hyperscalers acknowledging the constraint = signed PPAs and grid-equipment orders ramping. Compute side already in motion — confirms Q1 capex prints.

trade_setup: Watch SUBFLOW for IPP / nuclear / grid subthemes rotating into LEADING quadrant — that's the institutional money pivot.
Power-equipment names (GEV, ETN, PWR) often pre-front the IPPs — leading edge of the chain.
caveats: Power names already had a strong run — entry timing matters more than thesis confirmation.
Permitting / regulatory risk on nuclear/SMR is real; don't size them like compute names.

notes.headline: GOOGL +7% — market rewarding the most vertically-integrated AI story in mega-cap

stack_layers_owned.ads_engine: Google Ads (the cash engine still funding everything)

implications: Vertical integration premium: GOOGL monetizes inference at every layer (TPU economics → GCP margin → Gemini API → Search/YouTube ad surface). Few mega-caps own this many layers.
Margin compression risk for single-layer AI names: pure-play model labs and infra-only names get squeezed as integrated players capture spread across layers.
Re-rating dynamic: market is now pricing the full-stack flywheel rather than discounting GOOGL on Search-cannibalization fears.
Implication for SUBFLOW: 'AI Infrastructure' is too coarse — the vertically-integrated mega-cap subset deserves its own signal vs single-layer AI names.
